packages.name: nova
packages.description: Nova itself: the kernel and the system every app runs on
packages.title: Nova
packages.about:
Updates Nova on the disk it was installed on. The new version starts at the next restart; the one you have now stays in the boot menu as "Nova (previous version)", in case the new one misbehaves. Your apps, settings and files aren't touched.
A Nova running from a USB stick is updated by writing a new image to the stick.

changes.notes:
- wc and head pass any bytes; head -c N
- Reads and writes of 0 bytes succeed whatever the pointer, as on Linux
- publish.sh: NOVA_PUBLISH_ONLY publishes just the packages named
- btintel: room for the longest firmware name in its error
- Merge the menu bar, VLC and PhotoCraft branch; the menu bar is syscall 283
- Dolphin: the GameCube and Wii emulator as a package (roadmap 9.28)
- 200% writes both rows from the back buffer; nvidia -29: bottom halves keep the work identity
- Refresh rates: every rate of every mode, chosen in Settings and kept; nvidia -28 offers them
- The desktop shows a frame without the kernel lock, and enlarges it once
- What memory is used for (SYS_MEM_INFO, free -v); the kernel heap gives pages back
- A disk check at boot says so on the screen, with how far it is
- Lookups: ext2 remembers names and inodes, vfs_permit the folders above a path
- The block cache reads ahead: a miss fetches to the end of its 128 KiB group
- The block cache's index is taken as the cache fills, not whole at boot
- Steam: a launcher tile that starts the Windows Steam under Wine (steam 1.0-1)
- A signal handler doesn't run single-stepped; the trap flag comes back through sigreturn
- An open file's size is the file's, not what that open last knew

- A popup placed on the screen (NV_WIN_SCREEN)
- The block cache is a quarter of memory; a sliced read goes back to its program
- Long reads in slices, cheaper shadows, the USB service once a tick
- The stack report keeps its words off the thread's stack, and says it isn't safe yet
- A thread asleep inside the kernel sleeps even with a signal pending; the stack report costs programs nothing

- Wine: 32-bit DirectX games draw, smaller display modes, no blinking store page (wine 11.0-16)
- A click on a window over a desktop icon is the window's; libc can say where a stopped program is
- SYS_WIN_PUT at a place in the window; Vulkan surfaces drawn where their child window is
- A task doesn't go to sleep with a signal it would take pending
- mmap reads a file's range in big pieces before filling its pages
- ext2 reads neighbouring blocks of a file in one disk request
- L1: the profiler says what holds the kernel lock, and times input to the screen
- The desktop's processor's interrupts go ahead for the kernel lock too
- With four processors or more, the first is the desktop's alone
- The desktop goes ahead of the other processors for the kernel lock
- NVK sees the system memory that is free; wine 11.0-13, nvidia-vulkan 26.2.6-29

packages.name: nvidia
packages.description: NVIDIA's open GPU driver, for GeForce RTX 30 and 40 cards
packages.title: NVIDIA Graphics
packages.about:
NVIDIA's open-source GPU driver, for GeForce RTX 30 and 40 series cards (RTX 3050 to 4090). Nova loads it when it starts, if it finds one of these cards, and writes what it found to /var/log/nvidia.log.
With it, the browser draws pages on the card, Settings > Display can let the card drive the screen (a trial until you keep it), Task Manager shows the card's activity in its GPU tab, and Vulkan programs (the NVIDIA Vulkan package has two to try) use it for 3D.
If Nova ever stops while starting it, the next start skips it by itself (and says so), until a new version comes. modules=off in /etc/nova.conf turns every driver from a package off.

changes.notes: - Changing the resolution or refresh rate a few times in a row no longer turns off smooth frames (the screen synced to the monitor): each change was counted as a frame shown late, and after five the driver stopped syncing, leaving the desktop at about 66 frames a second whatever the monitor's rate.

- Fixes a warning in /var/log/nvidia.log that -27 brought back ("_rmGpuAllocLockIsOwner"): the interrupt's second step, now run from inside any wait, ran under the waiting program's name instead of the driver's own.

- Every refresh rate the monitor offers can be chosen in Settings > Display (with the Nova update of the same day): until now each resolution had one, and the monitor's own resolution only its own rate. Needs Nova 2026.11.18 or newer for the choice; on an older one nothing changes.

- Fixes the PC freezing when the monitor is turned off (or unplugged): the driver's handling of the display going away waited for the graphics card's lock, which the card's interrupt had handed to a second step that was queued behind that very handling and so never ran.
- Diagnostics only: a long wait for the card's lock also says what the driver itself has written down about who holds that lock.

- Diagnostics only: when the driver waits more than 2 seconds for one of its own locks, it says so at once in the kernel log, with which part of it took that lock last. The PC froze when its monitor was turned off, waiting for such a lock, and the report of the freeze could not say who held it.

- Fixes the "_rmGpuAllocLockIsOwner" line every start showed, and with it a way the driver could end up waiting for a lock nobody held: the second half of the card's interrupt handler, which on Linux runs on a thread of its own, ran on the waiting call's thread with the same identity, so the driver took it for that call and let go of the call's lock. It has its own identity now, as do interrupts (the identity Linux gives them, which Nova's desktop had shared).

- Diagnostics only: the driver's first few assertions and lock waits in /var/log/nvidia.log now say in what context they happened and which of the driver's functions led there, to find the cause of the "_rmGpuAllocLockIsOwner" line every start shows. Nothing else changes.

- Fixes -21, with which the card took 20 seconds longer to start and the screen stayed black: the driver's own waits for a signal were mistaken for locks and skipped, so a signal was lost. The driver's locks now behave as in -18, with the one difference that a wait given up on leaves the lock as it was, instead of leaving it off by one for good, which was the frozen desktop.

- Fixes -19 and -20, with which the card didn't start (a black screen; Nova then booted without the driver): the start waits for work of the driver's own, which -19 held back. The driver's work runs as it did up to -18; only a wait inside such work for a lock the interrupted call holds is passed at once instead of after 20 seconds.
- Every line of /var/log/nvidia.log now starts with the time since boot, so a log can say when something happened, not just in what order.

- The desktop no longer freezes for good after the driver gives up waiting for one of its locks (the log said "a semaphore stayed taken: carried on" every 20 seconds; seen after a monitor was switched off at an idle desktop). Work the driver hands off (its interrupts' second half, timers, queued work) no longer runs in the middle of a call that holds a lock it would need, and a wait given up on no longer leaves the lock off by one, which made every later wait time out too. The log line now says which thread, how many locks it held and how deep in waits it was.

- The screen no longer goes black for a few seconds (with the HDMI sound) when the machine is busy: a late frame is no longer taken as flips not working.
- Programs drawing on the card from several threads at once (the browser) no longer trip the driver's locks ("_rmGpuAllocLockIsOwner" in the log). Needs the Nova update published with it.

- The screen no longer tears: each frame of the desktop is shown at the monitor's refresh, so moving windows, scrolling, games and video are smooth. (-14 and -15 tried this and left the screen black: a function the driver lacks was called; fixed.) nvidia.flips=off in /etc/nova.conf goes back to the old way.

- Back to drawing straight on the screen, as up to -13: the flips of -14 and -15 left the screen black on some cards. They're off until they're known to work; nvidia.flips=on in /etc/nova.conf tries them.

- Fixes -14's black screen at start: if the card doesn't take a flipped frame within a quarter of a second, the desktop goes back to drawing straight on the screen (it may tear, but it works), and the log says why. The desktop no longer keeps programs waiting while a frame is on its way. Needs the Nova update published with it.

- The screen no longer tears: the desktop draws each frame out of sight and the card shows it at the monitor's refresh, so moving windows, games and video are smooth, at the monitor's own rate. Needs the Nova update published with it.
- In the Store for everyone with a GeForce RTX 30 or 40 card: no testing source to add first. The description says what the driver does now.
- Task Manager gets a GPU tab: how busy the card is (drawing, memory, video decoding and encoding), its video memory and its performance state. Needs the Nova update published with it.
- Programs can map system memory the card uses (it was refused as "not supported"): Vulkan (NVIDIA Vulkan's vktest) needs it to start the card.
- Programs can map the card's memory (video memory and system memory it uses) and write to it directly, as graphics libraries do; nvidia-info checks it. Needs the Nova update published with it.
- When the monitor is switched off and on again (or its cable unplugged and plugged back in), the picture comes back: the mode is set again.

- Settings > Display's resolutions go down as well as up (they were listed biggest first).
- Switches on the card's own sound device for HDMI and DisplayPort, so Settings > Sound can play through your monitor or TV (needs the Nova update published with it).
- Fixes the black screen: the display's output scale was left at zero, which turns every pixel black.

- If the display setup fails partway, the screen is given back to the old display instead of staying black.
- The last start's log is kept as /var/log/nvidia.log.1, and the log says more about each display step.

- The display: NVIDIA's display driver sets your monitor to its own resolution and refresh rate, and Nova's desktop draws through the graphics card. Settings > Display lists the monitor's modes.
- The first time, it's a trial: press Keep in Settings > Display. If the screen stayed black and you couldn't, the next start goes back to the old display by itself.
- Needs the Nova update published with it.

- Programs can talk to the driver: /dev/nvidiactl and /dev/nvidia0, as on Linux. The nvidia-info command (in the Terminal) asks it for the card's name, memory and the driver's version. Needs the Nova update published with it.

- When the driver waits for something another part of it does (its interrupt work, queued work, timers), that work now runs while it waits, instead of the wait being skipped. Waits that never end are logged with where they were.
- The card's interrupts are connected (MSI): the driver's check that they arrive stopped it before. Needs the Nova update published with it.
- First test: finds the card, starts NVIDIA's driver and the card's firmware, and writes what happened to /var/log/nvidia.log.

packages.name: nvidia-vulkan
packages.description: Vulkan and OpenGL for NVIDIA cards (Mesa's NVK and Zink, Google's ANGLE): vktest, gltest and zinktest check the card, vkcube and glcube spin cubes
packages.title: NVIDIA Vulkan
packages.about:
Vulkan, the 3D and compute interface, for GeForce RTX 30 and 40 cards: Mesa's open NVK driver, on NVIDIA's driver (the NVIDIA Graphics package).
Two programs to try in the Terminal: vktest lists the card, runs a small program on it, draws a triangle and saves it as vktest.png in your home folder (its last line says VKTEST PASS or what failed); vkcube opens a window with a spinning cube the card draws, and prints its frame rate; gltest draws a triangle with OpenGL ES through ANGLE, as the browser's WebGL does, and saves it as gltest.png (GLTEST PASS or what failed); zinktest draws one with OpenGL 4 through Mesa's Zink, as ported programs do, and saves it as zinktest.png (ZINKTEST PASS or what failed); glcube spins a cube with OpenGL in a window you can resize (F11: fullscreen), and prints its frame rate.

changes.notes:
- Memory can be mapped at an address the program chooses (32-bit Windows programs under Wine need it: they drew nothing).
- Vulkan functions are found by their older and newer names alike, as the usual loader does.
- A surface's picture can be stretched to the size its window shows it at, a picture made before its window exists is shown when the window comes, and a window inside a window no longer blinks.
- A Vulkan surface can show its picture at a place inside its window (Wine uses this for windows inside windows).
- Vulkan sees how much system memory is free (it thought a few megabytes), so programs that keep to its budget can use it.
- A Vulkan surface can be made before its window exists and find it later (Wine uses this).
- Vulkan can show its picture in a window that belongs to another program (a helper process drawing for the program that made the window).
- A program that uses Vulkan in two places at once (two instances) no longer ends when it closes the newer one first.
- Fixes Vulkan and OpenGL programs freezing now and then with their picture stopped (the graphics card could be told that work was finished too soon).

- Vulkan and OpenGL windows (vkcube, glcube) show a frame each time the monitor refreshes, in step with the desktop, instead of every 15 ms: no more dropped frames. Needs the Nova update published with it.
- The Store shows what each version changed (this list).
- OpenGL windows use colors a window can show (8 bits a channel), so glcube's cube appears instead of a blank window.
- Vulkan windows take images in RGBA order too, as OpenGL (Zink) asks for them.
- Programs that use the card from several threads at once (OpenGL in a window does) no longer get in each other's way.

- OpenGL in windows: glcube spins a cube in a window you can resize (F11: fullscreen; glcube -i: as fast as it goes).
- Vulkan windows follow their window's size when it changes. Needs the Nova update published with it.
- zinktest finds its OpenGL settings on the card (it found none).
- OpenGL (Zink) starts on the card: it stopped with "out of host memory".
- OpenGL for ported programs, through Mesa's Zink on Vulkan: zinktest draws a triangle with OpenGL 4 and checks it.
- gltest sets up the card's memory as the browser does, so the browser's WebGL starts instead of crashing.
- OpenGL ES through Google's ANGLE, as the browser's WebGL uses it: gltest draws a triangle and checks it.

- vkcube and other Vulkan windows show a frame each time the desktop draws one, instead of hundreds nobody sees.
- vktest no longer ends with two error lines from the driver.
- Vulkan programs that wait for the card with timeline semaphores (the browser's drawing) work.
- Programs that ask Vulkan for layers (the browser does) get an answer.
- vkcube's frame rate lines appear as they're printed.
- vkcube draws the cube's front faces (it showed the inside).
- Vulkan for programs, with windows: vkcube spins a cube in a window and prints its frame rate.
- vktest's shaders compile for the card.
- When vktest fails, it shows what NVIDIA's driver said.
- Vulkan can use the computer's memory for the card, as NVIDIA's driver requires.
- The card is set up the way Mesa expects.
- Vulkan's functions are all in place in a program (some were missing).
- vktest says where Vulkan stopped when it fails.

packages.name: steam
packages.description: Steam: starts the Windows Steam (installed under Wine) from the launcher
packages.title: Steam
packages.about: A tile for Steam in the launcher and the dock, so that it starts with a click and not from the Terminal. It starts the Windows version of Steam under Wine. Steam itself is not in this package: download SteamSetup.exe from store.steampowered.com and run it once with wine in the Terminal (wine ~/Downloads/SteamSetup.exe), and run wine --dxvk once so games use the graphics card. Steam's window takes up to a minute to appear; closed, it hides to Steam's icon in the top bar, whose menu has Exit Steam. Games need the NVIDIA driver and Vulkan packages. Early: some games work, many do not yet.

changes.notes: - Closing Steam's window hides it to its icon in the top bar, as on Windows: a click on the icon brings the window back, and Exit Steam in the icon's menu ends Steam. Needs Nova 2026.11.27.2027 and Wine 11.0-38.
- Closing Steam's window ends Steam, and Wine with it. It used to go on running where nothing showed it: on Windows it hides in the system tray, which Nova does not have yet. Needs Wine 11.0-26.

- Starting Steam again right after closing it works: the start used to fail twice and say so, because the Steam just closed was still going away and took the new one with it. The tile now waits for that to finish and tries again.
- New: a Steam tile in the launcher. It starts the Windows Steam installed under Wine, and starts it again by itself when the first start ends at once.

packages.name: wine
packages.description: Wine: run Windows programs (early: a command, no app yet)
packages.title: Wine
packages.about:
Runs programs made for Windows, 64-bit and 32-bit, in windows of their own with sound: type wine and the program's name in the Terminal (wine notepad, wine winecfg, or a .exe in your home folder).
The first start sets up a Windows folder in your home folder (.wine), which takes a few minutes.
DirectX through the graphics card (wine --dxvk) needs the NVIDIA driver and Vulkan packages.
This is an early version: games and Steam are not expected to work yet. It needs Nova installed on a disk, not started from a USB stick.

changes.notes: - A tray icon's menu closes on a click elsewhere every time, not only the first: a click on a tray icon now makes its program the active one, as Windows lets it, so the click away has a program to deactivate. Steam's menu closed once and then stayed open.

- A menu opened from a tray icon closes when you click the desktop, the top bar or another program, as on Windows: Steam's (which Steam draws itself) stayed open. The click makes no Windows program the active one and takes the menu's hold on the mouse away. Needs Nova 2026.11.27 (evening) or later.

- Windows programs' tray icons go in Nova's tray, at the top bar's right (Nova 2026.11.27 or later): their picture and tip; a click, double click or right-click goes to the program as on Windows. Steam's icon brings its window back on a click and shows its menu on a right-click.
- A program's popup menu or notification with no window of Nova's under it (Steam's menu from its tray icon, its window closed) is shown on the screen by itself; a click elsewhere closes the menu.
- `novamode tray` puts an icon in the tray and shows a menu on its right-click.
- Seen in the test machine with `novamode tray`; not yet with Steam on the owner's PC.

- A picture drawn before its window was there is shown as soon as the window is. It waited for the program's next picture of anything, and a program with nothing to draw (Steam, idle) kept a notification empty for a moment. The thread that reads a program's window events now looks every 5 ms while a picture is kept. Not testable without a graphics card; not yet seen on the owner's PC.

- A notification that is drawn before its window is there shows whole. Steam draws a toast once, 283 by 70, often a moment before Nova has its window; the picture was then cut to a 64 by 64 stand-in size, and when the window came only that corner, the icon, was shown, the rest seconds later when the toast was drawn again to fade. The picture now keeps the size the program asked for. Not testable without a graphics card: seen in the log on the owner's PC, the fix not yet seen there.

- A thread is no longer suspended or ended while it is inside Nova's memory allocator or writing to a stream. Stopped there it kept a lock every other thread of the program needs, the one that would resume it too, and the whole program stood still. Steam's graphics process was found so on the owner's PC (its window black, or stuck at its loading icon): its main thread suspended by Steam's own browser, which samples its threads, nine others waiting for the lock. This may be the black window Steam showed now and then at its start; that is not shown.
- `novamode suspend` suspends a busy thread 3000 times with work that needs memory before each resume.

- Notifications sit in the screen's corner again. Since 11.0-32 programs are told a work area smaller than the screen, and Steam put its toasts in that area's corner: 110 pixels above the bottom of the screen and 40 from its right edge, hanging in the air. One at the work area's right or bottom edge is now carried on to the screen's. On a screen narrow enough for the dock to reach the corner, the notification is partly behind the dock, as it was before 11.0-32.

- Notifications that slide in (Steam's toasts) are moved, not closed and made again at every step: they flickered, and were empty until the program drew into them again. Needs Nova 2026.11.27 or later; on an older Nova they are made again as before. Seen in the test machine with a test notification; not yet with Steam's.
- `novamode toast` shows a notification sliding up into the corner.

- Steam's Settings window opens on a low screen. It wants to be 720 high; on a screen that is 720 high (1080 lines at 150%) Nova made it lower, Steam put it back, and the window was made again without end: over a thousand windows, the pointer stalling, none to be seen. A window whose program insists on a size Nova had to cut down is now left as it is, showing as much as fits.
- Windows programs are told how much room a window can have on Nova (the work area: the screen less the top bar, a title bar and a margin), so that they fit their windows to it.
- The kernel log says when the game controllers' layer starts, offers a controller to Windows programs, and when one goes.
- `novamode tall` tries a window as high as the screen that refuses to be smaller.

- Game controllers reach Windows programs. Each of Nova's controllers (up to four) is offered as an Xbox 360 controller, the kind games and Steam know best, whatever the pad really is: buttons, sticks, triggers and the D-pad, and rumble back to the pad. Plugging one in or out while a game runs is noticed within a second. Seen with Nova's test pad and a test program; not yet with a real pad in a real game.
- `novapad` prints what Windows programs see of the controllers (`wine novapad 30 rumble`).

- Steam's library shows Play again by itself after a game is closed. Steam hides its pages while a fullscreen game covers the screen and looks again only when its window is made the active one; it was made active a moment too early, while the game's window still existed for Windows, so it stayed hidden (showing Stop) until clicked. It is now told once more after the game's window has gone.
- `novamode front` says which window Windows has in front, `novamode blink` shows a small window for a second.

- Each piece of graphics memory a program takes is no longer handed to a device file that is closed again at once (a step for sharing memory, which Nova doesn't do): about a millisecond and a half of every other program waiting, each time. Steam made a thousand such requests a minute.

- A program whose pictures are shown by another of its processes, with smaller views over the main one (Steam), no longer takes and gives back memory the size of its window for every frame, nor fills it a pixel at a time: less work for each frame Steam shows.
- The kernel log gets a line for every 600 frames a program shows through the graphics card, with how long their parts took.

- wineserver waits on its programs with epoll, which Nova has from 2026.11.21: it no longer looks at every Wine thread's connection each time anything in the system changes, which held up Steam's start. On an older Nova it goes on as before.
- A program started from a tile can be ended when its window is closed, where on Windows it would hide in the system tray and go on running unseen (the Steam tile uses this).

- A Windows program's window knows it is the active one when Nova gives it the keyboard because another program's window closed. Steam's library went on showing Stop after a game was closed, until it was clicked: its page was asleep, never told the window was in front again.
- Steam no longer stalls or ends when a game it started is closed: it stayed at "uploading 100%" for the cloud save, then went away minutes later. It called a graphics function Wine did not have.

- Games that turn the camera with the mouse work: while a game hides the cursor and keeps it in its window, Nova's pointer is locked there and the mouse's own movement goes to the game (the cursor used to stay visible and the camera jumped). A cursor a program hides is hidden.
- Keys, clicks and mouse movement reach Windows programs as they happen. They used to be picked up only ten times a second.

- Gunfire Reborn plays: its protection no longer takes the game for one being debugged and ends it. A program asking for its thread's debug registers (where a debugger keeps hardware breakpoints) was handed back whatever its memory held; they now read as zero, as they are.

- Windows programs see the PC's processors: their number, name and real speed (the registry's `CentralProcessor` keys were missing altogether, and the speed Wine would have given was a made-up 1000 MHz). Programs that tell the time from the processor's counter depend on it.

- Steam's notifications no longer flash in the middle of the screen when one arrives while Steam's own window is closed or minimized (a game starting): they go in the corner with another of Steam's windows, or are left out when it has none.
- Gunfire Reborn does not play yet after all: 11.0-19's fix is right, but the game's protection still ends it most of the time.

- A program signed with a certificate that has since expired is still found properly signed, as on Windows: the time stamped into its signature is what counts. Gunfire Reborn ended a few seconds into a level over this; it plays now.
- Steam's notifications really are popups in the screen's corner now: 11.0-17 looked for the wrong mark on them, and they still came up as windows in the middle of the screen.

- Steam's notifications are small borderless popups in the corner of the screen where Steam puts them, not windows with a title bar and a tile in the dock. Their place needs the Nova update published with it.

- 32-bit games drawn with DirectX show their picture: they were a black window (Crazy Taxi from Steam plays now).
- A game that asks for a screen size smaller than the screen goes fullscreen with its picture stretched to fit, instead of stopping when it changes the size.
- Steam's store page no longer blinks when the window around it redraws, and tooltips show their text.
- Programs that ask for Arial, Times New Roman, Courier New, Segoe UI or Verdana get Nova's Liberation fonts in their place: text in Steam's pages was missing where it fell back to them.

- Steam's store page no longer blinks: a window inside a window (the store is one) shows its picture where it is, not over the window's corner. Needs the Nova update published with it.
- Menus and drop-down lists drawn by the graphics card (Steam's) show their picture instead of a blank box.
- No more small white window named Explorer.exe: Wine's stand-in for a system tray isn't shown (Nova has no tray yet).
- Text drawn with DirectWrite shows: Steam's windows (and other programs built on Chromium) had no letters in them.
- DirectX programs get the system memory they ask for: the graphics driver thought only a few megabytes were free. Steam ended just after signing in because of it.
- Windows programs can check certificates and signatures and make secure (https) connections: Wine has GnuTLS now. Steam needs this to reach its logon servers.
- A program that prepares its picture before its window is shown (Chromium, so Steam's windows) shows it once the window is there, and keeps showing it when the window is resized.
